settings.title: Diagnostics
settings.subtitle: The app's recent log and device details. Copy or share the report to get help debugging.
settings.diagLine: The app's log, to get help
settings.updHelp: When Widgetkeeper gets new features, a short line about them is posted to Homey's Timeline after the update. Fixes are never posted.
settings.updEnable: Post new features to the Timeline
settings.varHelp: Homey doesn't let apps change variables, start flows, read dashboards or start Moods themselves. Make a key in the Homey web app under Settings → API Keys and paste it here. It stays on your Homey.
settings.varPermsTitle: What to tick on the key
settings.varForFlows: Flow Buttons, Keypad, and flows on Media's buttons
settings.varForCards: A speaker's own actions on Media's buttons
settings.varForStack: Smart Stack and syncing web dashboards (there's no permission for dashboards alone)
settings.varNoKey: The other widgets need no key.
settings.kpHelp: Codes for the Keypad widget: pick one in a Keypad’s settings. Only a fingerprint of each is kept, never the digits. Give each person their own: with Any code, the Flow card says whose was typed.
settings.kpRemoved: Code removed. Keypads that used it need another one.
settings.kpNameTaken: There’s already a code with that name.
settings.kpCodeTaken: Another code has these digits: each needs its own.
settings.kpMismatch: The two codes aren’t the same.
settings.kpNotACode: That isn’t one of the codes.
settings.kpLocked: Too many tries. Try again in __seconds__ s.
settings.kpFull: That’s as many codes as there can be.
settings.varSaved: Saved. The widgets can now change variables and start flows.
settings.varSavedVariables: Saved. The key may change variables, but not start flows.
settings.varSavedFlows: Saved. The key may start flows, but not change variables.
settings.varNotSet: No key saved: the widgets show variables and flows, but can't change or start them.
settings.varKeyScope: The API key may not change variables, start flows, read dashboards or start Moods: tick at least one of the permissions above.
settings.varKeyInvalid: The API key was not accepted.
settings.varDashboards: The Smart Stack can read dashboards.
settings.varNoDashboards: It may not read dashboards, which the Smart Stack needs: that takes the Homey permission.
settings.varSavedDashboards: Saved. The key may read dashboards for the Smart Stack, but not change variables or start flows.
settings.varNoMoods: It may not start Moods, which Light Controls' Room's Moods needs: tick Set Moods.
settings.varSavedMoods: Saved. The key may start Moods, but not change variables or start flows.
settings.namesHelp: How every widget shows device names. Widget settings, Flows and names typed on tiles stay as they are.
settings.namesSepHelp: Spaces count. A name without the separator shows in full.
settings.namesSepNeeded: Type a separator of 1 to 5 characters.
settings.namesNoneSep: No device name has “__separator__” in it.
settings.timeHelp: How every widget shows times. Automatic follows the language of the phone or browser that shows it.
settings.webHelp: Your Widgetkeeper widgets in any browser on your home network: a tablet, computer, TV or Nest Hub. Turn them on, add each screen below for its sign-in code, then build the dashboards on the page itself.
settings.webRemoteHelp: Use the web dashboards away from home too, on an encrypted address through Homey's cloud. Sign-in codes work there as well; a password is worth setting.
settings.webPasswordHelp: Optional: a password every browser enters once after signing in, most worth it with remote access on. Setting or changing it signs other browsers out; the screens above stay signed in.
settings.webPasswordSaved: Password saved. Other browsers must sign in again; the screens above stay signed in.
settings.webPasswordLocked: Too many wrong passwords. Try again in __seconds__ s.
settings.webPasswordForgot: Forgot it? The Flow card Remove the web dashboards password removes it.
settings.webScreensHelp: Each tablet, phone, computer or Nest Hub signs in with a short code of its own, made from an API key for that screen.
settings.webScreenStep1: In the Homey web app, go to Settings → API Keys and make a new key, named after this screen.
settings.webScreenStep2More: To change variables, start flows or Moods from it, also tick what the API key card above lists.
settings.webScreenRenewing: New code for __name__: paste its API key again, or a new one if you deleted its key in Homey.
settings.webScreenRemoved: Removed: its code no longer works. To sign the device out at once, also delete its API key in Homey.
settings.webScreenOnce: Type this code on the screen, or open an address below on it. It's shown only once; New code makes another.
settings.webScreenNoDevices: This key may not control devices, so the screen shows your widgets but can't switch anything.
settings.webScreenNeedName: Give the screen a name of at most __max__ characters.
settings.webScreenFull: That's as many screens as there can be (__max__).
settings.webBackupHelp: To back up or restore your web dashboards, open the web dashboards page and tap Settings in its side pane.

web.title: Web Dashboards
web.keyText: Enter this screen's sign-in code. Make one in the Widgetkeeper app settings under Web dashboards → Screens and browsers.
web.keyModeText: Paste a personal API key from the Homey web app (Settings → API Keys) with the Devices permission. It stays in this browser.
web.keyPlain: This address isn't encrypted: anything watching your home network could read the key. The Remote access address is encrypted.
web.screenCodeWrong: That sign-in code doesn't work. It may have been removed or replaced in the Widgetkeeper app settings.
web.screenCodeLocked: Too many wrong codes. Try again in __seconds__ s.
web.loadFailed: Could not reach Widgetkeeper on your Homey.
web.off: Web dashboards are turned off. Turn them on in the Widgetkeeper app settings in the Homey app.
web.offAway: Remote access is turned off. Turn it on in the Widgetkeeper app settings in the Homey app, or open this page on your home network.
web.name: Name
web.codeTitle: A Keypad code for editing this dashboard and going back to the dashboards
web.enterCodeLeave: Enter the code to leave this dashboard
web.codeLocked: Too many tries. Try again in __s__ s.
web.bgHardToRead: Text may be hard to read on this colour.
web.arrangeHint: Drag the dashboards to change their order or section.
web.tooManyWidgets: At most __max__ widgets on a dashboard.
web.forgetKeyText: Signs this browser out: it asks for a sign-in code again.
web.keepAwakeLock: The screen stays on while this page is open.
web.keepAwakeVideo: Uses a silent video to keep the screen on. If it still sleeps, turn off sleep in the device's settings.
web.dimText: Darkens the whole page, as if the screen were turned down.
web.dimScheduleText: By this device's clock. A Flow can dim too: the card Dim the web dashboards.
web.dimFlowNow: A Flow has set __level__ % for now. Moving a slider takes over.
web.rotateText: Shows the dashboards you tick in turn. A touch pauses it for a minute.
web.rotateEveryText: At least 10: a dashboard's widgets load again each time it shows.
web.backupText: The dashboards you choose in one file: their layouts, widgets, settings and the names typed on tiles. A restore brings back the ones you tick and leaves the others.
web.backupInvalid: This file is not a Widgetkeeper web dashboards backup.
web.backupTooMany: At most 64 dashboards: untick __count__ new ones
web.widgetTitleHint: Shown above the widget. Leave it empty for none.
web.passwordText: Enter the web dashboards password from the Widgetkeeper app settings.
web.passwordLocked: Too many tries. Try again in __seconds__ s.
web.sessionEnded: You were signed out. The password may have changed.
web.navHeld: This browser stays on this dashboard. Switching to another takes its code.
web.navNote: Drag the grips to change the order here. Hidden dashboards stay on the front page, and new ones show up here by themselves.
web.kioskHelp: For a kiosk browser: add ?kiosk=1 to the address to hide the bar, and &nav=1 as well to keep the side pane.
web.widgetsText: Everything you can put on a dashboard.
web.otherAppsKey: Other apps' widgets need an API key with full access (Homey) in this browser.
web.otherAppsFailed: Could not read other apps' widgets.
web.trustHint: Runs it outside the sandbox, for a widget that doesn't work in it. A trusted widget can read this browser's API key.
web.scaleHint: Lays it out at a phone's width and scales it to fill the column, so it wraps and sizes as on Homey's dashboard.
web.popupPictureFailed: The picture could not be loaded

about.electricity: Live power, the day's prices and your usage in charts.
about.thermostat: Three preset buttons for a thermostat or an aircon.
about.quickactions: Small tiles that switch a device with one tap.
about.sensoralarms: Tiles that turn red when a sensor raises an alarm.
about.sensordots: Motion, doors and cameras as a grid of dots.
about.roomhealth: Each room's temperature, humidity and air at a glance, yellow to red when one is off.
about.valuematrix: Devices or rooms against chosen values, green, orange or red by their range.
about.valueboard: Every value of the picked devices, by room or by device, as tiles or compact lines.
about.weather: The next 36 hours, hour by hour.
about.pollen: Today's pollen and the UV peak, for Europe.
about.heatmap: A week of any value as a weekday × hour heatmap.
about.cameras: Camera snapshots, with live video on a tap.
about.values: Any device value as a compact tile.
about.combined: One value of several devices as one: the average, the sum, the lowest or the highest.
about.flowtiles: Tiles your Flows write: a text or number, an icon, a colour and a fill.
about.lights: Light tiles with brightness and colour at hand.
about.lightrooms: Every room's lights on a card: switch a room, or open it for its lights and Moods.
about.sparklines: Values with a small chart of their recent history.
about.charts: How did it go? One value over any span, or against the period before or a second value.
about.totals: How much a value went up per hour, day or month: kWh, rain, hours of TV.
about.scatter: One value against another, a dot per hour: does the heat pump work harder when it's colder?
about.typicalday: Today's line over the usual day and its spread: is today unusual?
about.dailyrange: Each day's lowest to highest as a bar: how much did it swing?
about.compare: One value across devices, now and its range today, sorted: which room is warmest?
about.timeline: When was it on, open or moving? A row per value over the day.
about.stacked: Several values stacked on one time axis, the rest of a total as Other: who uses the power?
about.lines: Up to six values over time on one chart, a line each: every room's temperature side by side.
about.gauge: One value now on a bar or dial, green to red by level if you like: is the air still good?
about.variables: Variables as rows you can switch or change.
about.varpresets: Buttons that set a variable to preset values.
about.keypad: Buttons behind an optional code that start Flows or set a state.
about.flows: Start flows with a tap, in your colours and icons.
about.price: The electricity price now and in the coming hours.
about.timers: Kitchen timers that keep running on your Homey.
about.locks: Every lock and door at a glance.
about.curtains: Open, close or set curtains and blinds.
about.media: A speaker's music, volume and sources in one card.
about.clock: The time and date, with the weather now if you like.
about.textline: A note on a tile or a Post-it, typed in or written by your Flows.
about.spacer: Empty space to line up widgets in columns.
about.dayssince: Days since a chore was done, turning red when it's due.
about.stack: Widgets from another dashboard, taking turns.
about.shortcuts: Jump to your other web dashboards, in your colours and icons.
about.webpage: Any web page, scaled to fill the widget.
about.popups: Shows the popups that Flows send to its screen name here too.

web.syncText: Keeps this dashboard and one in the Homey app the same, both ways: on demand, when it's opened and every night. Homey's own widgets stay on Homey.
web.syncPreferText: When the same thing was changed differently on both since the last sync.
web.syncKeyScope: the API key needs full access
web.syncKeyInvalid: Homey no longer accepts the API key
web.syncKeyNeeded: Syncing needs a personal API key with full access (Homey) saved in the Widgetkeeper app settings.
web.syncNightlyText: Every synced dashboard, at this time on the Homey.
web.brandNameText: At the top of the front page and in the browser's title, in every browser.
web.brandIconText: Beside the name. One of the app's icons or a picture of your own.
